newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish hunters may kill more wolves this season.
newsitem.headline: Polish hunters may kill more wolves this season.

text.p: Polish forestry officials have more than doubled last year's limit on killing wolves due to the exceptional damage they have caused, PAP news agency said on Sunday.

"Between November 1 and the end of February hunters will be allowed to bag a total of 72 wolves in the province of Krosno," PAP news agency quoted a spokesman for the Regional Forest Authority as saying.
The 208 wolves living in the heavily-forested southeastern province so far this year have killed 308 stags, 183 roe, 80 wild boars and 230 sheep -- a big increase over 1995.
Last year, the kill limit for wolves was originally set at 92, but was slashed to 30 following pressure from ecological groups. Only 20 were actually shot, PAP said.
Retired French film star and animal-rights activist Brigitte Bardot has been among campaigners seeking a total ban on wolf hunting in Poland.
